To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Sustainable Seafood Movement has successfully created non-state market-driven fisheries governance tools to catalysing fisheries governance improvements; these tools are complementary to public governance efforts but there is a lack of coordination between the two sectors.

1) public and non-state market-based governance mechanisms have different objectives; 2) non-state market-based mechanisms have a greater ability to influence private actors; 3) non-state market-driven mechanisms have the ability to influence public governance mechanisms; and 4) there is a need for greater coordination and collaboration between these governance mechanisms.
1. Non-state market driven governance tools are not substitutes for public governance.
